name: Navigational tracking
plain: Passing IDs through link URLs or redirects when the person moves between sites.
meaning: Works even with third-party cookies blocked: site A appends an ID to the outbound link, site B reads it and sets a first-party cookie, or a tracker redirect sets its own first-party cookie for a moment. The main workaround to ITP and TCP.

web.api: URL query or fragment decoration; HTTP 302 redirect chains; first-party cookies

access.persistence: First-party cookie lifetime (Safari caps to 24 hours if set by script after tracker link decoration)
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can pass an ID along when you move between sites by link or redirect
limits.user_action: You click a link or get redirected to another site
can: Add an ID to the link's address
Pass the ID through a chain of redirects
Let the next site recognize you as the same visitor
cannot: Follow you if you type the address or use a bookmark
Work if the browser strips known IDs from links
See what you did on the first site beyond what is in the link
Last if you clear cookies and the ID is not stored
limits.differs: Firefox, Safari and Brave remove some IDs from links. Chrome does not.

story.what_it_is: Passing IDs in links or quick redirects as you move from one site to another.

marketing.name: Tracking prevention
marketing.pitch: WebKit documents how Safari fights tracking that uses link decoration and redirects.

story.for_you: You click a link and land on another site. You may not notice an ID in the web address or a flash redirect. The new site saves it in its own cookie, so third party blocking does not help.
story.for_makers: It is the main workaround for browsers that block third party cookies. IDs in links or redirects join your visit across companies. Browsers answer with caps on cookie life and stripping of known IDs.

use_cases.example: You click an ad and the ad network adds an ID to the link. The store saves it and ties your sale to the ad.
A site passes your visitor ID from its main site to its shop on another domain, to keep one session.
A game site sends you to a partner store with a code, so the partner can credit the referral.
A coupon site redirects you through a tracker so the store knows which coupon you used.
A login redirect passes a one time code between domains, which is not tracking but looks the same.
A newsletter link wrapper counts your click and then sends you to the story.

risks: Hard to see in the address bar

technical_bounds: Safari caps script-set cookies to 24 hours when the landing URL carries decoration from a tracker classified origin
Chrome bounce tracking mitigation deletes state of redirect-only sites
Cannot read the previous site's cookies

abuse: Cross-site ID passing after third-party cookies are blocked

history.change: ITP 2.1 capped script cookies to 7 days; ITP 2.2 capped to 24 hours when decoration present
Bounce tracking mitigation shipped for users with third-party cookies blocked
